podcast.title: "Sham Corporation" Ruling (1974)
podcast.body: A court ruled in 1974 that Five Platters Inc. was a "sham corporation" designed to unlawfully strip band members of their ownership in the band name, and that Book Ram had unfairly benefited. Subsequently, its trademark in "The Platters" name was declared void. "there was a court ruling back in 1974 that the whole purpose of five platters ink had been to illegally deprive the band members of their ownership in the band name, that it was a sham corporation."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Announced Retirement of Name (Pre-2011 Ruling)
podcast.body: Before the 2011 court decision, Five Platters Inc., under Jean Bennett's management, announced its intention to retire the name "The Platters." "Just before that ruling, five platters ink, which was now run by Jean Bennett, announced that they were going to retire the name."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Final Ruling: Never Owned the Name (2011)
podcast.body: In a definitive 2011 court ruling, it was determined that Five Platters Inc. had never legally owned the rights to The Platters' name, granting them instead to Herb Reed. "A judge finally ruled that Herb Read had the rights to the name, and that five platters ink had never owned the name."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Assignment of Name Rights by Members
podcast.body: At the time of its formation, the members of The Platters assigned any rights they had to the band's name to Five Platters Inc., a decision that led to decades of litigation. "The platters, at the time, assigned any rights they had to the platters, the rights they had to the band's name to this corporation."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Contesting Member Departures
podcast.body: In legal battles, Five Platters Inc. argued that band members mostly left because they were alcoholics unwilling to tour, and that they had willingly relinquished their rights to the band name. "five platters ink insisted that the band members had mostly left because they were alchoholics who didn't want to tour anymore, and that they'd given up their rights to the band name of their own free will."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Controlled by Book Ram
podcast.body: This corporation was established by Book Ram soon after The Platters signed to Mercury Records, with Ram maintaining control despite band members being shareholders. The purpose was allegedly to manage the band's rights, but it became a source of major legal disputes. "a corporation was set up, five platters ink, which was controlled by Book Ram, and had all the members of the platters as shareholders."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Run by Jean Bennett After Ram's Death
podcast.body: After Book Ram's death, his assistant Jean Bennett took over the operation of Five Platters Inc. "five platters ink, which was now run by Jean Bennett."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
